applied.problem: The 0.22 µF/km is a maker's typical figure for a 240 mm² 66 kV three-core cable, not String B's own data; and 'often described as capacitive' is a usage claim no source backs. Worded as typical, and as 'sometimes'.

C × U0² is the most a core holds when switched off at the peak of U0 in service, not the worst case overall: a VLF test at 1.5-2.5 U0 (lesson 5) or a high d.c. test can leave more. 'Peak of 38 kV' also reads as 38 kV peak; 38 kV is the r.m.s. U0.

Screen 3 calls C × U0² 'the worst case' without saying in service (a VLF or high d.c. test can leave more); 'peak of 38 kV' reads as a 38 kV peak; and 'Four things set how badly a shock hurts' is absolute where frequency, skin moisture and contact area also matter.
